dashboard.label: Gateway status cards show staged settings sync state, protocol toggle state, and last scan / commit timestamps.
Configured scrapers and bridges are listed here. Click Configure to jump directly to a device's setup screen.
Re-scan Configuration reloads config.cfg and protocol files without restarting. Rollback Configuration reverts to the last committed backup.

device__scraper_read_generic.label: Left panel shows the scraper's transport, bridge, protocol version, log level, and all active config key/value pairs. Changed values appear with an orange dirty-state dot.
Tabs switch between register maps (Holding, Input) and the JSON config editor. Each tab shows a summary of write (W), mask (M), and screen (S) counts.
Analyze button opens the register-map analysis tool to compare live device I/O against known protocols and queue register-map changes.

Protocol metrics table. W = write-back enabled, M = metric included in variable_mask (scraped), S = metric added to variable_screen (excluded from output). Address, variable name, unit, type, range, adjustments, and notes are shown for each register.

device__scraper_write_generic.label: Left panel shows the write scraper's transport, bridge, protocol version, log level, and all active config key/value pairs. Changed values appear with an orange dirty-state dot.
Tabs switch between register maps (Holding, Input) and the JSON config editor. Each tab shows a summary of write (W), mask (M), and screen (S) counts.

Protocol metrics table. W = write-back enabled, M = metric included in variable_mask (scraped), S = metric added to variable_screen (excluded from output). Address, variable name, unit, type, range, adjustments and notes are shown for each register.

device__bridge_generic.label: Left panel lists every config key for this bridge transport. Checked rows are actively set; unchecked rows fall back to the transport default shown in the DEFAULT column.
Connection summary shows transport type, endpoint (host:port), and live connection status (green = Connected).
Configuration summary lists all resolved key/value pairs that will be written to config.cfg on the next Commit.

create_device.label: Enter a unique name for this scraper section — written as the section header in config.cfg.
Choose the transport class (e.g. modbus_tcp, modbus_rtu). This determines which connection keys appear.
Link this scraper to a bridge or bridges (MQTT, TimescaleDB, etc.) so collected data is forwarded.
Select the protocol version whose register map this scraper will use (e.g. eg4_18kpv).
Select the default log level for this scraper (e.g. INFO, WARNING, ERROR).

analysis.label: Batch size controls how many registers are read per Modbus request. Click Run Analysis to start the live scan and score each selected protocol.
Select one or more protocol versions to compare against the live device scan. Check All selects every protocol at once.
Results panel shows match scores and queued register-map changes after analysis runs. Click Commit to apply queued changes to the protocol files.

protocols.label: Left panel shows the protocol name, group, available register maps (holding, input), and the source CSV file path.
Protocol register map editor. Each row is a register with editable variable name, doc name, unit, type, range, R/W flag, adjustments, and notes. Changes are staged and committed on demand.

protocol_json.label: JSON config sidebar lists available register maps and the current JSON config key/value pairs for this protocol.
JSON Config Editor — add, edit, or delete key/value pairs (string, number, boolean, or object). Save JSON writes the override file to the config folder; MPG loads it on next start.

read_mode.label: read_mode controls how MPG cycles through multiple transports: Sequential: one full pass per transport in order.  Concurrent: where all transports run in parallel threads. This mode is best for devices that do not share a common bus.  Interleaved: one block per transport in round-robin — best for shared RS485 buses.

logging-settings.label: backup_count sets the number of rotated log files to keep before deleting older log files.
Enable console/std-out in addition to file logging.
Interval: If using 1, the rotation occurs exactly at every single unit of your chosen time type.  In the screenshot, the chosen time type is weekly.  If 2, then every 2 chosen time type etc.
level sets the global log verbosity: DEBUG for detailed diagnostics, INFO for normal operation, WARNING/ERROR for quieter logs.
log_dir sets where logs are written which is useful for Docker volume mapping. Default compose file is synced to the "logs" default.
log file filename.  Default is MPG.log
Maximum log file size in bytes before rotation.  The setting on screen is roughly 100 megabytes.
rotation and when control log file rotation schedule (e.g. weekly on W0 = Monday). backup_count sets how many rotated archives are retained. max_bytes applies when rotation is set to 'size'.
W0 = Monday, W1 = Tuesday, W6 = Sunday

messages.label: General section: enabled is the master switch for all notification services. default_title is the fallback heading used when no title is supplied by the caller.
Send test message button fires a test notification through all enabled services to verify credentials.
Pushover service — enter your api_token and user_key from the Pushover dashboard. Values are masked for security.
Telegram service — provide the bot_token from @BotFather and one or more comma-separated chat_ids to receive notifications.

transport_library.label: All transport classes discovered in classes/transports/. Classification (scraper, bridge, base class) is shown alongside each transport's available config keys.

Scraper transports (blue badge) actively poll device registers on a schedule. Bridge transports (purple badge) receive and forward data. Base class rows are abstract parents not used directly in config.cfg.

transport_settings_trunc.label: Scan for New Settings re-reads the transport classes from disk and updates the registry, picking up any keys added after the last scan.
Consolidated alphabetical registry of every config key across all transport classes, showing which transports use each key and a plain-English description.

pages__help.label: SCREENS section lists every captured screenshot. Click an entry to view it with its annotations overlaid.
DOCUMENTATION section lists all files from the documentation/ folder, grouped by subfolder. Click to view markdown files rendered in-page or download other file types.
Right panel renders the selected screenshot (with annotation overlays) or the selected documentation file.

pages__about.label: Overview of MPG: an open-source data-collection middleware that bridges Modbus TCP/RTU hardware with MQTT, TimescaleDB, and InfluxDB.
Links section provides the GitHub repository URL for source code, issue tracking, and contribution.

pages__faq.label: Expandable FAQ entries cover core concepts (scrapers, bridges, dirty state, orphaned settings), common workflows (adding a device, editing protocol CSVs), and operational details (port number, restart requirement, backup location).

view_log.label: Log Output with up to 1,000 lines and a refresh button.
